set_d.instruction: Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below.
set_d.passage:
The U.S. Russia Sanctions Act, now signed into law by President Donald Trump, and its resultant impending tariffs, present a new and substantially different escalation of tensions between the U.S. and India. The law provides the U.S. President the authority to levy tariffs of up to 100% on countries such as India that import large quantities of Russian oil and gas. This is more serious than the penal tariffs that Mr. Trump had levied earlier. The escalation last year of reciprocal tariffs to 50% on India’s import of Russian oil was based on an Executive Order, and could be rescinded through the same method. This latest Act has been passed by the U.S. Congress and so carries a higher order of legal permanence and authority. Mr. Trump will have to justify in writing to Congress any waiver **he** wants to provide. The 50% tariffs hit Indian exports to the U.S. hard, but the impact was somewhat mitigated by exporters sharing the cost with their American customers. That was, however, a financially devastating and unsustainable bid to retain customers. Sharing a 100% tariff will be impossible for India’s largely micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) exporters. The 100% tariffs are also over and above the 10% ‘forced labour’ tariffs and the 50% Section 232 tariffs on steel and aluminium. Indian exports to the U.S. will simply become too uncompetitive should these new tariffs come to pass. India has three options before it: cut Russian oil imports, retain those imports and bear the tariffs, or convince the U.S. to implement a low tariff using the “up to 100%” phrasing of the law.

Continuing with Russian oil imports and bearing the tariffs would be a significant blow to India’s export ambitions and MSMEs. The U.S. is India’s largest export destination, accounting for about 20% of its total goods exports. In any case, historical data have shown that India has usually complied with U.S. pressure to cut oil imports from particular countries, including from Russia, vocal claims of strategic autonomy aside. Finding other sources will be difficult. Russia accounted for more than 51% of India’s oil imports as of July 2026, while supplies through the Strait of Hormuz remain constrained. India will have to **chivvy** countries such as Oman to hasten their expansion of alternative ports. The price of oil remains well above $100 a barrel, meaning finding favourable deals with new suppliers will be increasingly difficult. Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal will have much to do during his planned trip to the U.S. at the end of this month for the G-20 Trade Ministerial. There are still 30 days before the U.S. can levy its tariffs. India’s ability to secure a low rate will be a true test of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s friendship with Mr. Trump.

questions.question: According to the passage, which statement is true?
options: The United States accounts for approximately one-fifth of India's total goods exports.
The 50% reciprocal tariffs levied last year were passed directly by the U.S. Congress.
The U.S. President can grant tariff waivers without writing any justification to the U.S. Congress.
India currently imports less than half of its total oil supply from Russia as of July 2026.
questions.correct_answer: The United States accounts for approximately one-fifth of India's total goods exports.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'The United States accounts for approximately one-fifth of India's total goods exports.' is correct:** The passage explicitly states that the U.S. is India's largest export destination, accounting for about 20% (which equals one-fifth) of its total goods exports.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'The 50% reciprocal tariffs levied last year were passed directly by the U.S. Congress.': The text explains that the 50% reciprocal tariffs last year were based on an Executive Order, not passed by Congress.
• 'India currently imports less than half of its total oil supply from Russia as of July 2026.': The passage specifies that Russia accounted for more than 51% of India's oil imports, which is more than half.
• 'The U.S. President can grant tariff waivers without writing any justification to the U.S. Congress.': The passage clearly notes that Mr. Trump will have to justify any waiver in writing to Congress.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true according to the passage?
options: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal is scheduled to visit the U.S. for the G-20 Trade Ministerial.
The 100% potential tariffs would be levied in addition to existing forced labour and Section 232 tariffs.
India has historically refused to comply with U.S. pressure regarding oil imports from foreign nations.
There is a 30-day window available before the U.S. can officially levy the new tariffs.
questions.correct_answer: India has historically refused to comply with U.S. pressure regarding oil imports from foreign nations.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'India has historically refused to comply with U.S. pressure regarding oil imports from foreign nations.' is correct:** This statement is false according to the passage, which states that historical data show India has usually complied with U.S. pressure to cut oil imports from particular countries.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'The 100% potential tariffs would be levied in addition to existing forced labour and Section 232 tariffs.': The passage explicitly confirms these tariffs are over and above the forced labour and Section 232 tariffs, making this statement true.
• 'There is a 30-day window available before the U.S. can officially levy the new tariffs.': The text directly states that there are still 30 days before the U.S. can levy its tariffs, making this statement true.
• 'Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal is scheduled to visit the U.S. for the G-20 Trade Ministerial.': The passage confirms Minister Piyush Goyal's planned trip to the U.S. at the end of the month for this meeting, making this statement true.

questions.question: What does the highlighted pronoun in the paragraph refer to?
options: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal
President Donald Trump
The U.S. Congress
Prime Minister Narendra Modi
questions.explanation:
**Why 'President Donald Trump' is correct:** In the sentence "Mr. Trump will have to justify in writing to Congress any waiver he wants to provide," the pronoun 'he' directly refers to Mr. Trump.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal': Goyal is mentioned later in the second paragraph in a completely different context.
• 'Prime Minister Narendra Modi': Modi is mentioned at the very end of the passage and is not the subject of the sentence containing the highlighted pronoun.
• 'The U.S. Congress': Congress is the governing body to whom the written justification must be submitted, not the individual represented by the pronoun.

questions.question: What can be reasonably inferred from the passage?
options: Oman will immediately replace Russia as India's main crude oil supplier within the next 30 days.
Indian MSMEs will completely shut down all export operations to foreign nations if any tariff is imposed.
The price of global crude oil will permanently remain above $100 per barrel due to U.S. sanction laws.
India's strategic autonomy has not entirely prevented it from bowing to U.S. diplomatic and economic pressure in the past.
questions.correct_answer: India's strategic autonomy has not entirely prevented it from bowing to U.S. diplomatic and economic pressure in the past.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'India's strategic autonomy has not entirely prevented it from bowing to U.S. diplomatic and economic pressure in the past.' is correct:** The passage notes that despite vocal claims of strategic autonomy, historical data show India has usually complied with U.S. pressure to cut oil imports.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Indian MSMEs will completely shut down all export operations to foreign nations if any tariff is imposed.': This is an extreme over-generalisation not supported by the text, which only states that sharing a 100% tariff will be impossible.
• 'The price of global crude oil will permanently remain above $100 per barrel due to U.S. sanction laws.': The passage mentions the price currently remains above $100, but over-generalises by claiming it will permanently stay at that level.
• 'Oman will immediately replace Russia as India's main crude oil supplier within the next 30 days.': The text only states that India must urge Oman to hasten port expansion, over-generalising Oman's immediate ability to replace Russia.

questions.question: What reason does the author give for the stated issue?
options: It mandates an automatic 100% tariff on all goods exported by every Asian nation without exception.
It completely bans all diplomatic negotiations and trade ministerial meetings between the U.S. and India.
It permanently revokes the constitutional authority of the U.S. President to grant trade waivers.
It was passed by the U.S. Congress rather than issued via an Executive Order.
questions.correct_answer: It was passed by the U.S. Congress rather than issued via an Executive Order.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'It was passed by the U.S. Congress rather than issued via an Executive Order.' is correct:** The passage explicitly states that this latest Act carries a higher order of legal permanence because it was passed by the U.S. Congress, unlike last year's tariffs which were based on an Executive Order.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'It permanently revokes the constitutional authority of the U.S. President to grant trade waivers.': This is an exaggerated claim; the law still allows the President to grant waivers if justified in writing to Congress.
• 'It completely bans all diplomatic negotiations and trade ministerial meetings between the U.S. and India.': This is an exaggerated claim contradicted by the text, which mentions Goyal's planned trip for trade meetings.
• 'It mandates an automatic 100% tariff on all goods exported by every Asian nation without exception.': This is an exaggerated claim as the law applies specifically to countries importing large quantities of Russian oil and gas and allows tariffs "up to 100%".

questions.question: What is the meaning of the highlighted word as used in the passage?
options: nag or urge persistently
boycott officially
penalize economically
ignore completely
questions.explanation:
**Why 'nag or urge persistently' is correct:** In the context of "India will have to chivvy countries such as Oman to hasten their expansion", 'chivvy' means to pester, urge, or push persistently to get someone to act quickly.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'penalize economically': 'Chivvy' refers to persistent persuasion, not imposing financial or trade penalties.
• 'boycott officially': 'Chivvy' is about urging cooperation and action, whereas boycotting involves cutting off ties.
• 'ignore completely': This is the direct opposite of chivvying, which requires active, persistent engagement.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the elements mentioned in the passage?
options: While the earlier tariffs were authorized by Congress, the new 100% tariffs rely solely on an Executive Order.
While the 50% tariffs reduced oil prices, the 100% tariffs will force crude oil prices down below $100.
While exporters managed the earlier 50% tariffs by sharing costs with customers, sharing a 100% tariff is impossible for Indian MSME exporters.
While the earlier 50% tariffs only targeted steel exports, the 100% tariffs apply exclusively to aluminium.
questions.correct_answer: While exporters managed the earlier 50% tariffs by sharing costs with customers, sharing a 100% tariff is impossible for Indian MSME exporters.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'While exporters managed the earlier 50% tariffs by sharing costs with customers, sharing a 100% tariff is impossible for Indian MSME exporters.' is correct:** The passage directly compares the earlier 50% tariffs (where exporters shared costs with customers) with the proposed 100% tariffs, which MSME exporters cannot possibly share.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'While the earlier 50% tariffs only targeted steel exports, the 100% tariffs apply exclusively to aluminium.': This is an under-generalisation that misrepresents Section 232 tariffs and the scope of the new oil-related tariffs.
• 'While the earlier tariffs were authorized by Congress, the new 100% tariffs rely solely on an Executive Order.': The passage states the exact opposite: earlier tariffs relied on an Executive Order, whereas the new Act was passed by Congress.
• 'While the 50% tariffs reduced oil prices, the 100% tariffs will force crude oil prices down below $100.': The text does not state that tariffs caused reductions in oil prices.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: The Complete Rescission of Executive Orders by the U.S. Congress
Section 232 Tariffs: A Success Story for Indian MSME Exporters
How Oman Expanded Its Ports to Control Global Crude Oil Supplies
Navigating the Tariff Storm: India's Dilemma Over U.S. Sanctions and Russian Oil
questions.correct_answer: Navigating the Tariff Storm: India's Dilemma Over U.S. Sanctions and Russian Oil
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Navigating the Tariff Storm: India's Dilemma Over U.S. Sanctions and Russian Oil' is correct:** This title accurately reflects the main focus of the passage, which centers on India's strategic options amidst impending U.S. tariffs on Russian oil imports.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'How Oman Expanded Its Ports to Control Global Crude Oil Supplies': This incorrectly assigns a minor supporting detail about Oman to be the central subject of the entire passage.
• 'The Complete Rescission of Executive Orders by the U.S. Congress': This assigns a legal mechanism mentioned in passing as the primary topic of the text.
• 'Section 232 Tariffs: A Success Story for Indian MSME Exporters': This incorrectly describes Section 232 tariffs as a success story, whereas the text emphasizes severe financial strain on MSMEs.
